onScreenGraphic.headline:
18 New School Streets
Approved Across Southwark
onScreenGraphic.body: Southwark Council has voted to expand timed traffic restrictions outside eighteen primary schools.

timeline.voiceoverText: Southwark Council has voted to establish eighteen new School Streets, restricting non-resident motor traffic during drop-off and pick-up hours.
timeline.citationFooter: SOURCE: Southwark Environment & Transport Committee · 20 Nov 2025
citations: Southwark School Streets Expansion Report, Para 1: '18 additional primary schools approved'

data.excerptPrefix: "Timed pedestrian and cycle zones shall operate 8:15–9:00am and 3:00–3:45pm, with
data.highlightPhrase: full exemptions for Blue Badge holders and residents

onScreenGraphic.headline:
Full Blue Badge & Resident
Access Preserved
onScreenGraphic.body: Automatic camera enforcement targets through-traffic while protecting disabled and local access.

timeline.voiceoverText: Under the statutory traffic order, automatic camera enforcement targets rat-running commuters while guaranteeing full exemptions for Blue Badge holders and local residents.
timeline.citationFooter: SOURCE: Traffic Management Order TMO 2025/11 · Clause 3.2
citations: Clause 3.2: 'full exemptions for Blue Badge holders, emergency vehicles, and registered zone residents'

onScreenGraphic.headline:
34% Drop in Gateside
Nitrogen Dioxide Levels
onScreenGraphic.body: Over seven thousand four hundred pupils across Peckham and Camberwell gain safer walking routes.

timeline.voiceoverText: Air quality monitoring shows existing zones cut school-gate nitrogen dioxide by thirty-four percent, with the expansion protecting over seven thousand four hundred pupils daily.
timeline.citationFooter: SOURCE: Southwark Air Quality Monitoring Network · 2025 Audit
citations: Air Quality Audit Section 4: '34% reduction in NO2 at school gates; 7,400 pupils covered'

pillars.desc: Signage & camera activation from Spring Term
Warning notices only during first 4 weeks
360 new secure school bike & scooter racks
Living ivy pollution barriers along playgrounds

onScreenGraphic.headline:
Four-Week Grace Period
Before Fines Begin
onScreenGraphic.body: Rollout includes living green screens and 360 new cycle racks alongside a four-week warning period.

timeline.voiceoverText: The Spring Term rollout includes a four-week grace period with warning letters only, alongside three hundred and sixty new cycle racks and playground green screens.
timeline.citationFooter: SOURCE: Southwark Highways Implementation Schedule · Para 6
citations: Para 6: 'Four-week warning notice grace period; 360 cycle spaces and living green screens'
